result.rationale: The controller does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first; host.destroy` with no nil check, so a nonexistent or already-deleted id raises NoMethodError and returns a 500.

judged_text: destroy calls host.destroy on a possibly-nil record when the id does not exist, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500. Double-delete of the same host (e.g. retry after a timeout) produces a 500 instead of idempotent success or a 404.

record.issue_text: [BUG] destroy calls host.destroy on a possibly-nil record when the id does not exist, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500. Double-delete of the same host (e.g. retry after a timeout) produces a 500 instead of idempotent success or a 404.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, both `update` and `destroy` fetch the record via `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without handling the `nil` case. In `destroy`, it immediately calls `host.destroy` (and in `update`, `save_host(host)` dereferences `host`), which will raise `NoMethodError` when the id does not exist (e.g., double-delete/retry), resulting in a 500 instead of an idempotent success or a 404.
